summary: The purpose of IP addresses and MAC addresses in delivering packets, and the roles of the main application protocols HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, FTPS, SMTP and POP3.

blocks.content: A **logical address** given to every device on a network (and on the Internet) so that data packets can be **routed to the correct device**. It can change when the device moves to another network.

blocks.title: IPv4 and IPv6
rows: 8 groups of 4 hex digits separated by colons

blocks.content: A **physical, unique 48-bit address** burned into a device's network interface card by the manufacturer, written as 6 pairs of hexadecimal digits, e.g. `3C:52:82:1A:9F:04`. The first half identifies the **manufacturer**, the second half the **device**.

blocks.title: IP vs MAC
rows: Logical, assigned by the network (DHCP) or manually
**Switches** — to deliver frames to the right device **within a local network**

blocks.title: How a packet reaches a device
items: Data is split into **packets**; each packet has a header with the **source and destination IP addresses** and a sequence number.
**Routers** read the destination IP and forward each packet along the best available route; packets may take different routes.
When the packet arrives in the destination LAN, the router finds the MAC address of the device with that IP (using **ARP**).
The **switch** uses the **MAC address** to send the frame to the correct port.
The destination device reassembles the packets in order using the sequence numbers.

blocks.content: A set of **rules** that devices must follow to communicate: the format of data, how it is sent, received and checked for errors.

blocks.title: Application-layer protocols
rows: Transfers web pages from a web server to a browser
HTTP **encrypted** with SSL/TLS — protects passwords and payment data; the server is authenticated with a certificate
Uploads and downloads files between a client and a server (e.g. uploading a website)
**Sends** email from a client to a mail server and between mail servers
**Downloads** email from the server to one device (usually deleting it from the server)
Reads email **kept on the server**, synchronised across devices

blocks.content: Email: **SMTP sends**, **POP3/IMAP receive**. Secure versions (HTTPS, FTPS) **encrypt** the data so it cannot be read if intercepted.
